title: What does a materials prediction target cost? Distinct labels and error certificates on a common test population
abstract: We reconstruct distinct cumulative training labels for two acquisition strategies across 150 property-seed pairs in a public materials regression benchmark. We derive conservative certificates for the error on any subset from the full-library MAE, RMSE and subset size, accounting for the rounding of the archived metrics. On arm-specific unmeasured materials we certify sixteen first-crossing cost advantages for cluster selection. On exactly the same never-acquired materials at every budget and for both arms, one ordering is certified. In that QM9 case the two strategies first reach the target with 100 and 561 distinct labels on a common test population of 122,398 molecules. The other 149 common-population comparisons remain unresolved.
